newsitem.title: JORDAN: King Hussein rebukes Jordan's unions over protests.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein rebukes Jordan's unions over protests.

text.p: King Hussein on Tuesday rebuked Jordan's professional unions which rallied to support journalists protesting against reporting restrictions in an amended press law.
The official Petra news agency quoted the king as saying that unions not directly affected by the press law should concentrate on supporting their own members.

"God willing, the time will come when everyone will mind their own work and business," the king said at a ceremony in north Jordan marking the start of Israeli water supplies from the Sea of Galilee to Jordan.

The leaders of four professional unions -- lawyers, engineers, dentists and writers -- resigned in protest at the press law, which imposed sweeping restrictions on reporting and stiffened fines for offenders.

The heads of nine other professional unions have also threatened to step down. But the journalist union's board members withdrew their resignation last week to give the government more time to discuss the law.
King Hussein said he did not want to see "an official from the veterinary union threatening his resignation or declaring a protest against amendments in the press law".
"I don't understand the connection between vets and journalists," he said.
